en.tldr: You pick the main model with an alias (sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, best, opusplan) or a full model name that pins a version. Several sources can set it, and the highest-priority one wins. To get a stronger model only at key moments, configure an advisor instead of switching the main model.
whenToUse: Switching between Sonnet for routine work and Opus for hard reasoning
Pinning an exact version so alias updates don't move you
Planning on Opus and implementing on Sonnet with `opusplan`
Letting Claude consult a stronger model at decision points with `/advisor`
keyFacts: `/model <name>` saves the choice to `model` in your user settings; pressing `s` in the `/model` picker switches for this session only.
`--model` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` apply only to the session you launch with them.
Aliases resolve to the recommended version per provider and change over time; pin with a full name like `claude-opus-5-5`.
`opusplan` uses `opus` in plan mode and `sonnet` for execution.

Resumed sessions keep the model they were using, not your current default.

The advisor requires the Anthropic API; it is not available on Amazon Bedrock, Google Cloud's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry.

The other model runs a whole delegated subtask, not just consultations at decision points.

questions.stem: A team lead wants every developer who clones the repository to start Claude Code sessions planning on Opus and implementing on Sonnet. Developers should not need to run any command or edit their shell profile. What should the lead do so it applies to everyone who clones the repo?

options.text: Ask each developer to run `/model opusplan` once
options.why: It saves the choice to each developer's user settings; nothing is shared through the repo, and each person must run it.
The advisor is consulted at decision points; the main model stays the same and doesn't switch between plan and execution.
Project settings travel with the repo, and `opusplan` uses Opus in plan mode and Sonnet for execution.

options.text: Add `export ANTHROPIC_MODEL=opusplan` to the README setup steps
options.why: An environment variable lives in each developer's shell, so it needs manual setup per machine.

questions.explanation: The requirement is a shared, zero-step default for everyone who clones the repo. A `model` value in the project's `.claude/settings.json` is committed with the code and applies at every launch. `opusplan` is the alias that plans on Opus and executes on Sonnet. `/model opusplan` would also select the right alias, but it saves only to each person's user settings.
keywordCues: planning on Opus and implementing on Sonnet
not need to run any command

questions.stem: Mid-session on Sonnet, a developer wants to try Opus on the current task. Their saved default must stay Sonnet for future sessions, and they don't want to quit the running session. What should they do?

options.why: Typing `/model <name>` behaves like Enter in the picker: it also saves Opus as the default.

options.text: Open `/model` and press `s` on the Opus row
options.why: `s` switches the model for this session only and leaves the saved default unchanged.
It keeps the default, but it requires quitting and relaunching the session.
It adds an advisor and saves `advisorModel`; the main model stays on Sonnet.

questions.explanation: Two constraints decide it: keep the saved default and stay in the running session. In the `/model` picker, `s` switches for this session only. Typing `/model opus` saves Opus as the default, and `--model` needs a new launch. The advisor doesn't change the main model at all.

options.why: Escribir `/model <name>` equivale a Enter en el selector: también guarda Opus como default.

options.text: Abrir `/model` y presionar `s` en la fila de Opus

Conserva el default, pero obliga a salir y relanzar la sesión.

questions.stem: A developer runs a long refactor on Sonnet. Most turns are routine, but they want a stronger model's input before Claude commits to an approach and whenever an error keeps recurring. options.text: Switch the main model with `/model opus`
options.why: Every turn would run on Opus, which raises cost on the routine work.

options.text: Create a subagent with `model: opus` for the refactor
options.why: Opus would run the entire delegated subtask, not only the decision points.
Claude consults the Opus advisor at key moments it chooses, while Sonnet handles the routine turns.

That is the advisor tool: Sonnet stays the main model and calls Opus before committing to an approach or when stuck. `opusplan` switches only at the plan-mode boundary, and a subagent or `/model` would run Opus for far more than the key moments.

The advisor setting chooses the consulted model, not the main session model.

questions.stem: Which CLI flag launches Claude Code on a given model for that session only, without changing your saved default?
questions.explanation: `claude --model <alias|name>` sets the model at startup for the session you launch with it. It ranks just below `/model` in priority and doesn't write to your settings, so it is also how you run different models in different terminals at the same time.

es.stem: ¿Qué flag del CLI lanza Claude Code con un modelo dado solo para esa sesión, sin cambiar tu default guardado?
es.explanation: `claude --model <alias|name>` fija el modelo al arrancar para la sesión que lanzas con él. Está justo debajo de `/model` en prioridad y no escribe en tus settings, por eso es también la forma de correr modelos distintos en terminales distintas a la vez.

questions.stem: Order these ways of setting the model from highest to lowest priority.
